title: Audio timing attached to props edited while the audio was made
body:
## Summary
The audio job merged its timing into whatever props version was latest when it finished, so an edit landed during the job got a timing measured on other scenes.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:164 reads props vN; generation runs for minutes; apps/server/src/projects.ts:116 attachTiming merged into latestProps() at that moment. Registry concurrency-guards / preparation-is-the-staleness-window: a verdict read at fetch time must be re-checked before the irreversible write. Fixed: attachTiming(id, timing, measuredOn) refuses when the latest version differs; pipeline passes propsRow.version.

## Flow
- Produce starts on props v1
- owner saves a JSON edit (v2) or the co-pilot calls set_props
- audio finishes -> attachTiming stored v3 = v2 + v1's timing
- fixed: job fails 'props changed while the audio was made (v1 -> v2); produce again'

## Expected impact
The preview never plays cues measured on other scenes. Could break: a produce racing an edit now fails and must be re-run (intended).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stored timing always describes the stored scenes
Before: stale attach stored as v3 (test red)
After: refused, nothing stored; same-version attach stores v3
Method: gate - projects.test + pipeline.test (version argument pinned, red when dropped)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Publish job re-uploaded a render that was already published
body:
## Summary
publishJob uploaded the latest/pinned render whatever publications it already had; the one-publication rule lived only in the studio.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:406-445 had no publication check; the studio's scheduleOffered (apps/studio/src/studio-logic.ts) is the only guard. A double click, a second tab, or a calendar slot after a direct publish made another private video and spent upload quota. Registry concurrency-guards / idempotency-by-design. Fixed: Refusal when the render has a publication in the current publish mode (dry does not block live).

## Flow
- POST /publish twice for the same render
- two jobs, two uploadVideo calls, two publications
- fixed: second job 'refused' naming the publication

## Expected impact
No duplicate private uploads. Could break: a deliberate re-upload now needs a new render (none exists in the flows).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one upload per render and mode
Before: 3 publish runs -> 3 uploads (test red)
After: 1 upload, 2 refusals
Method: gate - pipeline.test publish block
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: apps/server/src/pipeline.ts publishJob: publications where render_id = render.id and mode = modes.publish -> Refusal

title: Job cancel signal not passed to the ElevenLabs client and loudness runs
body:
## Summary
Carried card (Audio & Music r16): the pipeline never handed ctx.signal to ElevenLabsClient, normalizeTo or measureLoudness.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:169, :297, :303. The audio package accepts signal since d7fe97c / 920ec25. Fixed by passing the job signal at all three sites. Registry subprocess-lifecycle.

## Flow
- cancel during a TTS request or the loudness passes
- before: waited for the call
- after: the request / ffmpeg run is aborted

## Expected impact
Cancel returns in milliseconds during generation and mastering. Could break: nothing (cancel already handled between steps).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - cancel reaches in-flight work
Before: opts.signal undefined at 3 of 3 sites (tests red)
After: 3 of 3 receive the job AbortSignal
Method: gate - pipeline.test with ffmpeg faked through promisify.custom
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/pipeline.ts ElevenLabsClient({..., signal: ctx.signal}); normalizeTo({..., signal}); measureLoudness(video, { signal })

title: Asset rows took the run's plan tier instead of the take's recorded tier
body:
## Summary
Carried card (Audio & Music r16): every asset row got the run's tier, ignoring the generation-time tier generate.ts records.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:234 plan_tier: planTier. Fixed to a.plan_tier ?? planTier ?? null: a recorded tier wins; an unrecorded one (fixtures, pre-92e1f6b cache) keeps today's fallback, so replay e2e and fixtures are untouched. Whether unknown should deny is a separate Lane C card.

## Flow
- free-plan take in cache, account now starter
- produce -> row/manifest said starter
- fixed: row says free; gate sees free

## Expected impact
A free take reused after an upgrade can no longer pass the monetized gate. Could break: nothing for unrecorded takes (same fallback).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - asset rows carry the generation-time tier
Before: ['starter','starter'] (test red)
After: ['free','starter']
Method: gate - pipeline.test audio run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/pipeline.ts asset insert plan_tier: a.plan_tier ?? planTier ?? null; packages/audio/src/generate.ts:54 generatedPlanTier

title: render_keyframes before set_props returned an empty success
body:

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:150-151. Registry mcp-tools / tool-schema-design, law failure-not-empty-success. Fixed: Refusal('render_keyframes', 'project <id> has no props yet; call set_props first') - MCP isError, replay {error}, REST 422; PipelineApi unchanged.

title: setProps stored a timing block that timed other scenes
body:
## Summary
Carried card (Compose & Render Gate UI): the JSON editor round-trips the stored timing; setProps accepted it after scenes were reordered, added or dropped.

## Description
apps/server/src/projects.ts:102-112 stored whatever validated; the schema does not cross-check timing against scenes. Fixed: errors[0] 'timing: it times scenes ... but the props have ...; remove the timing block' when the timing's scene ids are not exactly the props' scene ids in order. The editor-side strip stays with the studio card (Lane B there).

## Flow
- after a Produce open JSON, reorder scenes, Save
- before: stored; preview plays the old cues
- after: refused with the remedy

## Expected impact
Stored timing never lies about the scenes. Could break: a JSON edit that keeps the timing must now drop it (the next Produce re-times anyway).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - stored timing matches stored scenes
Before: 2 of 2 mismatches stored (test red)
After: 2 of 2 refused; matching timing accepted
Method: gate - projects.test without the warehouse
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/projects.ts setProps timing/scene id comparison; e2e/fixtures/llm/cd4f7d4ade65d0bffd52472c.jsonl: 0 of 2 set_props carry timing

title: Query tool failed a valid SELECT ending in a line comment
body:
## Summary
Warehouse.query wrapped the statement on one line; a trailing '-- comment' swallowed the closing paren.

## Description
apps/server/src/warehouse.ts:169 `select * from (${sql}) limit`. 'select ... -- note' and 'select ...; -- note' passed the guard and then failed with 'Parser Error: syntax error at end of input'. Fixed: wrap on own lines, drop a trailing ';' with any line comments after it; the guard still parses the original.

## Flow
- co-pilot sends an annotated SELECT
- before: parser error, a wasted turn
- after: rows

## Expected impact
Fewer confusing tool errors. Could break: nothing (the guard is unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - valid guarded SQL runs
Before: 2 of 2 commented queries fail (test red, real warehouse)
After: 2 of 2 return rows
Method: gate - warehouse.test
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Assets with no recorded plan tier still inherit the run's tier
body:
## Summary
After e2ecad2 a take with no recorded tier (pre-92e1f6b cache, replay fixtures) is still stamped with today's subscription tier.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts asset insert falls back to planTier. packages/audio/src/generate.ts:50-53 says an unrecorded tier 'gets none, and the publish gate denies it'. Denying would be the honest record (rights-and-provenance: grants are not retroactive), but every legacy cache hit would then fail the monetized gate and need a paid regeneration, and replay fixtures carry no tier (18 of 18) so the replay e2e would need plan-tier.json as an explicit fixture source. Owner call: spend and fixture policy (CLAUDE.md: ElevenLabs credits).

## Flow
- decide: deny unknown tiers, or attest the run tier for legacy entries with a manifest note
- if deny: replay keeps plan-tier.json as the fixture tier; live legacy takes regenerate

## Expected impact
Decides whether old takes can be monetized. Could break: live re-produces of existing projects (spend).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no tier is claimed that was not recorded
Before: unknown -> run tier
After: unknown -> denied (predicted; spends credits on legacy takes)
Method: simulation - walked generate.ts and the fixture metas; the decision is spend, not a measurement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
evidence: e2e/fixtures/audio/*.json: 1 of 19 files mention plan_tier (plan-tier.json itself); packages/audio/src/generate.ts:50-53
instrument: owner decision; then pipeline.test: unrecorded tier -> null row and gate deny

title: Keyframe seconds past the video end are clamped silently to the last frame
body:
## Summary
render-worker.mjs clamps every requested second into the composition and returns the clamped still as if it were the asked one.

## Description
apps/server/src/render-worker.mjs:52 frame = min(durationInFrames - 1, round(s * fps)). Asking for 70 s on a 45 s video returns the last frame (twice for two late seconds, same file name), with no note - the model critiques a frame it did not ask for. Fix: report the frames actually rendered (seconds in, frame out) or refuse out-of-range seconds with the duration.

## Flow
- render_keyframes [10, 70, 80] on a 45 s video
- stills: [f300, f1349, f1349]
- model reads three different moments

## Expected impact
The co-pilot knows which moments it saw. Could break: callers that index stills by position.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a still is the frame asked for or says it is not
Before: out-of-range seconds clamped silently (read)
After: named per frame (predicted)
Method: simulation - worker needs a Remotion bundle + browser to run; not reachable in a sweep round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: stills job with frames beyond durationInFrames on the real bundle: count stills whose frame != round(s*fps)

title: Calendar ready list offered projects the scheduler refuses
body:
## Summary
Carried card (Compose & Render Gate UI, calendar.ts side): ready() excluded renders on the calendar, schedule() refuses any project with a live slot.

## Description
apps/server/src/calendar.ts:83-91 vs :137-138. After a re-render, the project reappeared as ready and schedule() answered 'already on the calendar'; the existing test pinned that dead offer. Fixed: ready() also excludes projects with a live slot (pin strengthened, old expression forbidden). The studio scheduleOffered/ProjectDetail half stays the studio's Lane B card.

## Flow
- slot on r1, re-render r2
- before: Calendar lists p1/r2 as ready, scheduling fails
- after: not listed; the slot's drift + reschedule re-points it

## Expected impact
The Calendar never offers a refused action. Could break: nothing (cancel frees the project again, tested).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - offer matches acceptance
Before: ready() = [p1/r2] while schedule throws (test red)
After: ready() = []; after cancel [p1/r2]
Method: gate - calendar.test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/calendar.ts ready(): live set from LIVE statuses

title: Calendar tick swallowed per-slot and read failures without a trace
body:
## Summary
Held-over Server Core card: tick() had two bare catches; a failing slot never fired and said nothing.

## Description
apps/server/src/calendar.ts:188 and :218. Registry scheduling / schedule-observability (every decision not to fire leaves evidence). A corrupt stored verdict or SQLITE_BUSY (the generation worker shares app.sqlite) left error null until the missed window. Fixed: read failure logged; per-slot failure writes 'the scheduler could not process this slot: <cause>' to slot.error and logs it with the slot id; retry and other slots unchanged.

## Flow
- due slot whose render verdict is corrupt
- before: never fires, error null, no log
- after: error on the slot + '[calendar] slot <id>' log

## Expected impact
'Why did my slot not fire?' has an answer on the Calendar. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - failures leave a trace
Before: error null, 0 log lines (test red)
After: error names the parse failure, 1 log line, other slot dispatched
Method: gate - calendar.test
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Style management half-wrote for archived heroes and all-archived styles
body:
## Summary
StyleLibrary.update validated against all items while list() skips archived ones.

## Description
apps/server/src/library.ts:102-121 with the route passing board.list({status:'all'}) (apps/server/src/app.ts:257). An archived hero was stored then silently replaced; a style whose items are all archived got its override written and then update() returned undefined, the route's s.id threw, the owner saw 400 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. Fixed: both refused before writing, ArchivedError -> 409.

## Flow

- before: row written + 400 TypeError; after: 409 'restore one of its items first'

## Expected impact
No phantom writes or misleading 400. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of a style's live items
Before: archived hero accepted (test red); all-archived -> undefined
After: both refused, board_styles empty
Method: gate - library.test
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Calendar scheduler and retention timers are not on the shutdown roster
body:
## Summary
Held-over Server Core card: main.ts starts setInterval(calendar.tick) and startRetention, serve.ts's makeShutdown gets no stoppers.

## Description
apps/server/src/main.ts:59-61 create the timers; apps/server/src/serve.ts:15-25 passes no `stoppers` (apps/server/src/shutdown.ts:11 supports them). A tick between stopJobs and closeDb can claim a slot and enqueue a publish into a runner that is shutting down; after closeDb it throws into the (now logged) catch. Fix lives in Server Core (main.ts returns the timers or a stop(); serve.ts passes them as stoppers). Out of this round's paths.

## Flow
- SIGINT during a due minute
- stoppers [] -> tick still armed while jobs stop
- fix: clearInterval first

## Expected impact
Shutdown never races a publish claim. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - timers stop before jobs and the DB
Before: 0 of 2 timers on the roster (read)
After: 2 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - out-of-scope files (main.ts, serve.ts)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: shutdown.test: build main's parts, run shutdown, assert no calendar.tick after stopJobs (fake timers)

title: schedule() accepts a publish time the tick will immediately mark missed
body:
## Summary
schedule()/reschedule() accept a publish_at older than the missed window; the next tick turns the new slot 'missed'.

## Description
apps/server/src/calendar.ts:130-149 and :155-164 validate only that publish_at parses; apps/server/src/calendar.ts:199-201 marks anything overdue past missedWindowMs as missed. A mistyped date (last year) creates a slot born missed. Fix: refuse publish_at < now - missedWindowMs in both doors. Not built: needs an injectable clock (CalendarService has none) and every existing calendar test schedules at fixed 2026-09-30 dates against the real clock - a test migration, M.

## Flow
- schedule with publish_at 2025-10-01
- 201 Created, then 'missed' within 30 s
- fix: 400 naming the window

## Expected impact
The Calendar refuses what it would immediately abandon. Could break: tests using past fixed dates (migrated with a clock).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - accept only what can fire
Before: past-window publish_at accepted (read)
After: refused (predicted)
Method: simulation - a test needs a clock seam; M with test migration exceeds this round's build size
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: calendar.test with an injected clock: schedule(now - window - 1 min) throws; existing tests pass the clock

title: Unreadable warehouse snapshotted and cached an all-untested heatmap
body:
## Summary
capabilities() read every error as 'no transform has run yet'; a transient failure became a trend snapshot and the day's cache.

## Description
apps/server/src/heatmap-service.ts:42-50 bare catch -> []. On the first read after a start, a DuckDB lock/IO error produced 88 cells with nothing tested, stored as a snapshot and cached until a newer evaluation or the next UTC day. Registry error-handling (a failure must not read as empty). Fixed: only DuckDB's missing-table Catalog Error (both wordings) means 'nothing tested'; anything else propagates, nothing cached or snapshotted.

## Flow
- server starts while the warehouse read fails
- before: all-blocked heatmap stored + cached
- after: error now, real cells on the next read

## Expected impact
The feasibility map and its trend never show a phantom collapse. Could break: /api/heatmap and /api/sources answer 500 during a real warehouse failure (honest).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failure is not 'no data'
Before: probe: 88 cells, 0 tested, 1 phantom snapshot, recovered read still cached 0 tested
After: rejects, 0 snapshots, recovered read has tested cells
Method: gate - heatmap-service.test + probe
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Malformed capabilities.yaml silently disabled every freshness window
body:
## Summary
stalenessWindows() caught parse errors as 'no spec file', so stale passes counted as fresh evidence.

## Description
apps/server/src/heatmap-service.ts:14-23. A YAML typo (or a mapping instead of a list) returned an empty window map; max_staleness_days null everywhere; a cell could read 'go' on months-old evidence (fail-open on a gate input). Fixed: only ENOENT means no windows; a parse failure or non-list throws naming the file.

## Flow
- owner edits pipeline/capabilities.yaml and leaves a brace open
- before: heatmap silently loses staleness
- after: heatmap errors naming the file

## Expected impact
Staleness cannot be switched off by a typo. Could break: the heatmap is unavailable until the yaml parses (intended).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - fail closed on a gate input
Before: malformed yaml -> resolved, windows null (test red)
After: rejects naming the file; missing file still resolves
Method: gate - heatmap-service.test with a temp repo root
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Videos ledger ids were 32-bit; a collision dropped or failed a row

apps/server/src/topics-migrate.ts:89 and apps/server/src/topics.ts:121. Two renders sharing a prefix lost a ledger row on every backfill; a recordVideo PK collision threw after the render was committed. Registry migrations / idempotent-steps. Fixed: whole render id / whole UUID.

title: metricsOverview runs one metrics_daily query per publication
body:
## Summary
N+1: a select per publication inside the map.

## Description
apps/server/src/metrics.ts:51 runs `select ... where publication_id = ?` for each publication returned by the join at :45-49. Harmless at today's handful of dry publications; linear in publications once live uploads and daily pulls exist. Fix: one query ordered by publication_id, date, grouped in JS.

## Flow
- GET /api/metrics with N publications
- N+1 queries
- fix: 2 queries

## Expected impact
Metrics screen cost stays flat. Could break: ordering within a publication (keep date order).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - queries per metrics read
Before: N+1 (read)
After: 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - no query counter on the Db in tests; S instrument not built this round (budget went to defects)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: metrics.test with 50 publications and a wrapped db.select counter: queries == 2
